transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-03 15:00 PT | Duration: ~48m | Recording: auto | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood Partner Ops), Ethan (Caldera Head Cloud Partnerships), Sofia (Caldera Solutions Architect), Marcus (Caldera Procurement), Diane (Caldera CTO)

Summary: quick intros, partner go-to-market model discussion, technical constraints (VPC, data residency), pilot scoping and success metrics, next steps and action items.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining today, really appreciate you making time. i'm jordan reyes from redwood inference, ae on the partnerships team. we've got priya and ava with me. how's it going on your side?
[00:20] Ethan: hey jordan, good to meet you all. ethan here from caldera cloud. big fan of the product, been poking around the hosted api. excited to see if a reseller path makes sense for us.
[00:28] Sofia: hi, sofia - solutions arch. we run a marketplace for managed infra and are exploring adding inference offerings through partners.
[00:34] Priya: great, thanks. quick note — i'll be the technical lead on our side for the pilot. we'll talk through performance guardrails and the KV cache behaviour.
[00:45] Diane: morning, Diane here. i'm mostly listening today but wanted to hear procurement and SSO / security bits.
[00:50] Marcus: and i'm marcus, procurement. i'll need the timeline and contract overview.

[01:05] Jordan: perfect. agenda: 1) understand caldera's go-to-market and margin expectations, 2) deployment patterns—hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC, 3) pilot scoping and success criteria, 4) commercial model & enablement. sound right?
[01:20] Ethan: yep, that covers it. quick background: we sell managed cloud infra to mid-market SaaS and also have channel customers (MSPs). typical procurement cadence is 60–90 days. margins we target depend on whether the offering is white-label or marketplace listing.

[02:02] Priya: can you say more about expected QPS and latency targets for your average customer? are you targeting synchronous chat endpoints, or async batch embedding workloads?
[02:18] Sofia: mostly synchronous chat and some reranking for search. typical peak is 800–1.2k QPS for smaller deployments, but per-customer baseline is 50–200 qps. latency target is sub-200ms token time end-to-end for UI flows — we know that's tough.

[02:48] Jordan: ok, that's helpful. our hosted API has routes that can hit low latency, but for the scale you describe i'd expect two viable partner models: 1) reseller listing where caldera resells Redwood hosted (fastest launch), or 2) dedicated pools / private deployment in caldera's VPC for tighter SLAs and data isolation.
[03:10] Ethan: what are the trade-offs re: unit cost and latency between those?
[03:18] Priya: brief—hosted: lowest time-to-market, simpler billing, but multi-tenant and some rate limits. dedicated: you get reserved capacity and predictable throughput (and often better p95 latency due to less noisy neighbors), but it needs committed spend and longer lead times. private VPC: you manage the infra side, we ship a control plane — best for data residency and compliance but integration work is higher.
[03:50] Marcus: procurement will care about committed minimums for dedicated — what are typical contract sizes?
[03:58] Jordan: typical Dedicated minimums vary; for mid-market resellers we often see quarterly reserved commitments in the tens of thousands per month USD; for large enterprise partners it's negotiated. we'll send benchmarks.

[04:20] Sofia: a couple of technical Qs: 1) We need SSO for partner portal and RBAC for resellers. 2) Any KMS/HSM integrations for key management? 3) How is audit logging surfaced?
[04:35] Priya: we support SAML SSO, RBAC at token and route level, and we integrate with external KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have HSM options for Private deployments. Audit logs are available via the console and can be forwarded to SIEMs — we'll attach the security whitepaper.
[04:58] Ethan: do you have SOC2 or ISO?
[05:02] Jordan: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, yes. we'll attach certs and SOC pack.

[05:25] [Small crosstalk]
[05:40] Priya: on the pilot: I want to align on what success looks like. sample plan: 4-week pilot with 2 caldera-managed customers, measure p50/p95 latency, token cost per request, error rates, and quality regressions on a small eval set. thoughts?
[06:05] Sofia: sounds right. can we include a cost model for different batching and quantization profiles? our customers care about unit economics.
[06:14] Priya: yes — we'll share Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching, quant profiles by workload. note: quantization can change quality subtly so we tie it to eval prompts.

[06:40] Jordan: for GTM, do you want co-branded landing pages or white-label?
[06:46] Ethan: initial prefer marketplace listing + co-marketing. after pilot, if traction is strong, we may do white-label bundles.

[07:05] Marcus: commercial — can you send a reseller margin table? we need to model MSP margins vs marketplace cut.
[07:12] Jordan: yes; i'll send bands. typical is X% discount to reseller depending on committed volume — we'll detail that.

[07:30] Priya: technical deep-dive — Sofia mentioned synchronous chat with sub-200ms token times. two knobs: 1) model variant (smaller/larger), 2) batching and prefix caching. if you host in our Dedicated or Private VPC mode you get more control over pre-warmed KV cache warm-up.
[08:01] Sofia: what's the suggested pilot model set? we want predictable cost but good quality.
[08:09] Priya: suggest starting with a mid-sized open model we have vetted on the catalog for latency/cost balance, with an option to fall back to a smaller quantized variant during spikes. we can run a set of perf runs on your traces.

[08:40] Diane: security question — for Private VPC, how are keys managed and is there data egress from our VPC to Redwood's control plane?
[08:52] Priya: control plane communicates over customer-controlled endpoints; data plane stays in your VPC for Private deployments. keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM and we never persist raw customer inputs in hosted if opted out — these are configurable. I'll mark the exact tech note to share.

[09:22] Ethan: are there existing partners doing similar reseller deals we can reference?
[09:28] Jordan: yes — we recently onboarded two channel partners in APAC; i'll share anonymized case studies and an onboarding checklist.

[10:00] [15s pause for link share] Jordan: putting links in the chat: partner pack, security whitepaper, sample contract.

[10:18] Sofia: great — on the pilot scoping, we need to lock the number of pilot customers and runbooks. what telemetry will you provide? token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, and error traces?
[10:32] Priya: exactly — plus per-request tracing and sampled request payloads (redacted), and token cost breakdown by route/model. We'll provide a dashboard access for the pilot.

[11:00] Marcus: procurement question — lead times for dedicated capacity procurement? how long to spin up a dedicated pool?
[11:08] Priya: typical lead time is 2–6 weeks depending on region and GPU availability; sometimes quicker if we have existing pool capacity. We'll include capacity SLAs in the doc.

[11:40] Ethan: curious about marketplace billing — do you handle billing through you or is it passthrough to our billing?
[11:48] Jordan: two options: Redwood bills Caldera and you bill end customers (reseller), or we can integrate marketplace billing where the cloud marketplace handles end-customer charges and we settle with you. details depend on region and tax.

[12:20] Sofia: any constraints around model licensing if we want to include some proprietary models?
[12:28] Jordan: model licensing varies; for open-models in our catalog it's straightforward. For third-party licensed models we handle legal gating. If you want hosted private models we can onboard with a licensing addendum.

[12:55] Priya: quick note — if you plan to route some traffic to customer-run on-prem nodes, we need to define fallback logic and compatibility (sequence length, kv cache semantics). mixing runtimes is possible but increases complexity.
[13:18] Sofia: understood. we want to start simple — hosted reseller first, then extend to Dedicated and Private VPC for a subset of customers.

[13:40] Jordan: ok pilot framing: 4 weeks, 2 customers, baseline run with your traces, perf bench, and evaluation on a 50–100 prompt eval set. success criteria: p95 latency under your target for at least 80% of traffic, cost per 1k tokens within expected band, and no critical security blockers.
[14:05] Ethan: that seems reasonable. what's the expected Redwood involvement during pilot ops?
[14:12] Priya: we'll provide a SE point-of-contact for onboarding, a runbook for KV cache warmups, and a Slack channel for realtime troubleshooting. Ava will handle partner enablement and GTM assets.
[14:36] Ava: i'll put together a go-to-market checklist — co-branded assets, launch announcement template, joint webinar idea.

[15:00] [Jordan shares a sample partner onboarding checklist link in chat]
[15:10] Marcus: re: legal — will you accept our standard reseller addendum or do you have a partner agreement template?
[15:18] Jordan: we have a partner T&C and reseller agreement; we'll send a redline-friendly version. we'll also include data processing addendum and SOC docs.

[15:45] Sofia: for the perf runs, can you take a sample of our traces now and give a ballpark?
[15:52] Priya: yes — after the call send two days of token-level traces (sanitized) and we'll run them through a lightweight perf harness. we'll produce a small report with suggested batching / model variants.

[16:18] Ethan: timeline-wise, if we get the partner packet early next week, procurement can move in parallel; we'd like to kick pilots mid-March. is that realistic?
[16:28] Jordan: yes — if partner packet and PO are in place, pilot mid-March is doable.

[16:42] Diane: one more compliance check — our customers in EMEA require data residency in EU. can you support region-restricted deployments?
[16:52] Priya: yes, we support region pinning and private deployments in EU regions. we'll note region-specific SLAs.

[17:10] [Short discussion about support SLAs and escalation path]
[17:30] Jordan: recap and next steps: jordan to send partner packet + pricing and T&Cs by Friday (Mar 5); priya to run perf harness once traces are received and share checklist by Mar 10; caldera to choose 2 pilot customers and share traces by Mar 12; marcus to confirm procurement timeline and preferred contract template by Mar 9; schedule tech deep-dive week of Mar 15.

[18:05] Marcus: noted. any blockers on our side?
[18:10] Sofia: just coordination internally. will fill in the traces and target customers.

[18:28] Jordan: great — final note: i'll include case studies and a sample POC SLA. also attaching the security pack in the follow-up.
[18:40] Ethan: thanks everyone. excited to move forward.
[18:45] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and links.
[18:52] [meeting ends — informal chatter and hangup]
